consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has astigmatism, which means her eyes don't focus properly on things. It's been a challenge for her, especially when trying to read or watch TV. We're really worried about how this might affect her learning.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: She had fluid in her ear for a while, and we were so scared it would affect her hearing permanently. Luckily, after treatment, everything seems back to normal now. But I still get anxious whenever she complains about her ear.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing has been an issue for her since she started eating solid foods. Some foods are just too hard for her to manage. We've had to adjust her diet accordingly to make sure she can eat comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist says she needs regular check-ups to monitor her heart health. I try to stay on top of these appointments because I know how crucial they are for her well-being. It's always a relief when the results come back normal.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, she's been slower than her peers to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting. It was worrying at first, but with therapy and support, she's making progress. I'm just eager for her to catch up.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures can be a real issue for her. She's very picky and will only eat certain things if they're prepared in specific ways. Mealtime can be challenging, but we're learning to navigate her preferences.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Yes... two main concerns. Firstly, her fontanelle took longer than usual to close completely. And secondly, her speech development isn't where it should be for her age. She doesn't speak as much as other children her age. Both these things worry me and I hope we can find ways to support her better.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart health monitoring due to a previously identified heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, particularly with chewing harder foods, and has a strong aversion to certain food textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and is slower to achieve certain milestones such as walking and sitting compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in the ear, which was treated successfully and has since returned to normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have experienced issues with fluid in the ear, including otitis media and glue ear, which can affect hearing.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision and makes reading and watching television challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia or hypermetropia, which may impact their daily activities.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with chewing, especially with harder foods, and requires periodic dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups and treatments.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shown variability in educational attainment, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support in mainstream settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, but some children with smaller ANKRD11 deletions may have more significant problems that are unrelated to other genes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and is slower to reach milestones such as walking and sitting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome have developmental delay and various behavioral differences.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can cause an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart health monitoring and monitoring of her fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes. Additionally, some individuals may experience tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Monitoring for tethered cord should be considered in children with significant anomalies of the roof of the mouth (palate) and if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns. 

Note: N/A indicates that the information is not applicable to this specific patient.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects how she sees objects at different distances. She sometimes struggles with focusing, especially when looking at things close-up. 

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child had fluid buildup in her ears a couple of times. It affected her ability to hear clearly and caused discomfort. Thankfully, after treatment‚ it cleared up‚ but we monitor her ears regularly now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem prone to chipping or breaking easier than they should. Even minor accidents can cause noticeable damage‚ so we have to ensure she’s extra careful during meals and playtime to avoid any incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Compared to other kids‚ she tires out faster during physical activities. While she can run around and have fun‚ we notice she needs breaks sooner than her friends do. It might be related to her overall energy levels rather than a specific heart condition‚ but we keep an eye on it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: Unfortunately‚ she falls more frequently than other children her age. Whether it’s due to coordination or balance issues‚ we’re working with her to improve strength and agility to reduce these incidents.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been challenging for her since infancy. Certain textures and tastes make mealtime difficult‚ and she has sensitivities to particular foods that trigger digestive discomfort.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues‚ our child moves slightly differently compared to her peers. There’s also a concern regarding delayed fontanelle closure‚ where certain bones in her skull took longer to fully close than typically expected. These aspects require periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care accordingly.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out faster than other kids her age during physical activities, suggesting potential heart-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties since infancy, with sensitivities to particular foods and textures triggering digestive discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves slightly differently compared to her peers and has delayed fontanelle closure, requiring periodic assessments to monitor progress and adjust care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid buildup in her ears and has had difficulty hearing clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her vision and allows for occasional blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and requires regular dental check-ups to prevent tooth decay and other issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth can break or chip更容易，因此需要定期的口腔检查和护理。

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires out faster than her peers during physical activities, indicating potential challenges in maintaining focus and engagement in classroom settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some may require more support and some benefit from a specialist setting.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves slightly differently and has delayed fontanelle closure, which may impact her overall development and movement patterns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may benefit from therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle), and some may have hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
   - Regular dental check-ups
   - Regular hearing reviews to age 5
   - Ophthalmology review
   - Palatal review
   - Skeletal review (wrist, hip, spine)

b) Recommendations for treatments:
   - Addressing fontanelle closure delays
   - Monitoring and treating scoliosis
   - Managing tethered cord
   - Treating hip dysplasia
   - Considering endocrine investigations for suspected hormonal imbalances

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and struggles with swallowing and vomiting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to be clumsier than her peers and has trouble with balance and coordination, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient frequently rubs her eyes and has difficulty focusing, possibly indicating underlying vision orocular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate, which can affect speech development and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision difficulties such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus), which may impact her daily life and school performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and astigmatism, and may also experience squint or strabismus.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits due to various issues, including weak enamel and possible tooth sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth size and positioning can vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, and some may experience weak enamel, making proper oral hygiene尤为重要。

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows variability in educational attainment, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring support in mainstream settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, individuals with KBG syndrome can range from needing support in mainstream settings to achieving qualifications, with a small percentage demonstrating greater independence.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including speech delay and clumsiness.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Generally, individuals with KBG syndrome may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences, with some showing more pronounced challenges than others.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis, and delayed fontanelle closure, adding to her health concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletally, some individuals with KBG syndrome may have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and delayed fontanelle closure, which are additional factors to consider.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular monitoring for her heart valve issue, periodic dental care, and ongoing assessment for potential palatal abnormalities and tethered cord issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Overall, individuals with KBG syndrome may require ongoing monitoring for various health conditions, including heart, palate, and neurological issues, ensuring early intervention helps mitigate risks and improve quality of life. Regular dental check-ups, periodic heart evaluations, and comprehensive assessments for palatal abnormalities and tethered cord issues are crucial for this condition. Additionally, managing feeding difficulties, ensuring adequate nutrition, and considering speech therapy and physical therapy can further enhance the child's development and wellbeing. Monitoring growth velocity and identifying any concerning trends allows for timely interventions to address potential hormonal imbalances or other systemic issues that may arise. By combining a holistic approach to care with close collaboration between parents, healthcare providers, and specialized therapists, children with KBG syndrome can achieve greater independence and lead fulfilling lives despite their unique set of challenges. This collaborative care model ensures that each child receives personalized attention and support, maximizing their potential and improving their quality of life.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when engaging in physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced feeding difficulties since birth, showing trouble eating certain foods and occasional discomfort after meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences staring spells that last for a few seconds without explanation, indicating potential neurological concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to loud noises and gets frustrated in crowded or noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and speech delays, with some experiencing subtle anomalies of the palate and delayed fontanelle closure.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, requiring glasses to correct vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to prevent and treat tooth decay and cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding has been tricky since day one, and the patient has trouble eating certain foods, suggesting possible dental or feeding concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed extra help in school, with some children needing EHCP and others staying in mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some developing into adults with varying levels of independence and abilities.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences staring spells and lacks clarity in speech, which may indicate developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with some showing significant delay and others acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, including constipation and diarrhea, and has difficulty finding foods that agree with her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures that are controlled by medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in her ear and has noticeable different posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and subtle anomalies of the palate, which can affect speech development and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods and needs regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common in KBG syndrome, and some children may require short-term tube feeding.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty with academic tasks and requires additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, but some children with smaller ANKRD11 deletions may have more significant problems that are unrelated to other genes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable different posture when standing or walking and is being monitored for potential palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with delays in milestones such as rolling, sitting, walking, and using cutlery, zips, and buttons.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which may lead to an increased curvature of the spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some children may experience subtle anomalies of the palate.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, regular hearing reviews to age 5, eyesight (ophthalmology) review, check position of testes in boys, consider a palate review, consider a cardiac review following diagnosis, consider a skeletal review in children following diagnosis, consider review and investigation for tethered cord, monitor growth velocity if height is below the 2nd centile, consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Speech therapy, physical therapy, behavioral therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in her heart, which is being monitored closely.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced slow weight gain compared to her peers, suggesting potential feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, which can be alarming, and she also has a speech delay, which is being addressed through therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often turns the volume of the TV up very high, indicating possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have speech delay, and hearing loss and subtle palate problems can worsen speech delay.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, which can be alarming, and may indicate a potential visual issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and tooth issues are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced slow weight gain compared to her peers, suggesting potential challenges in academic performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some go to a mainstream primary school and others may require more support and may need to attend specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, which can be alarming, and she also has a speech delay, which is being worked on through therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) Recommendations for screening:

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness more quickly than peers, suggesting potential cardiac involvement, possibly related to overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, with some days being better than others, managed primarily through diet changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes of staring off into space, which can be concerning and lead to rest periods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced glue ear in the past.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, or strabismus, which can affect his eyesight and lead to discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and breaks or chips easily, requiring frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Teeth can be prone to breaking or chipping, and weak enamel is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences delays in development and learning, requiring additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require more support and resources to facilitate their learning.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and lacks clarity in speech, affecting his communication abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, and some may exhibit behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can cause scoliosis, and delayed closure of the soft spot on his head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and delayed closure of the soft spot on the head (anterior fontanelle).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups, has speech delay, and experiences tiredness more quickly than peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have various cardiac, neurological, and hormonal concerns, including heart valve abnormalities, tethered cord, and hormonal imbalances, which should be monitored and treated as per specialist advice.

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... our son has been having trouble seeing the board at school, and it's really worrying me. He often squints and leans forward to try and get a better look, which is affecting his posture and overall classroom experience.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Well, we've noticed he seems to pick up on some sounds just fine, but then misses others completely. It's like he's tuning in and out, and we're concerned it might be impacting his learning or social interactions.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: The dentist said his tooth enamel is weak, which makes me nervous about cavities and how to best care for them. I ensure he brushes regularly and avoids too many sweets, but I worry it might not be enough.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, the cardiologist found a structural abnormality in his heart. We're waiting for further tests to understand what it means long-term, but for now, we're just monitoring and trying to reduce any strain on his heart through lifestyle adjustments.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Our child has hypotonia, which means his muscles are overly tight. Physical therapy is helping, but it's a challenge to find activities he enjoys that don't exacerbate the condition.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He can be quite picky about food and will often refuse certain meals, which worries me about his nutrition and whether he's getting everything he needs for growth and development.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Actually, yes... he has speech delay, and it's been a significant concern for us. Also, there's an issue with his hip - dysplasia, which affects his mobility and comfort level. We're working with therapists to address both these issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored closely to determine if it requires surgery or can be managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences slow weight gain and has trouble eating, making meal times frustrating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids her age, tripping over her own feet sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hearing and eyesight seem to be slightly off, as she doesn't always respond when called and has difficulty seeing clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and speech delays, with some experiencing subtle palate abnormalities and undescended testes.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to various tooth problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome, with many babies requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding and occasional need for dental interventions.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient appears to be generally behind other children in development, with noticeable lag in play and interaction abilities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most children with the condition attend mainstream primary schools.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often and seems to develop slightly slower than peers overall.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature in KBG syndrome, with varying levels of educational attainment and levels of independence upon reaching adulthood.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, which can lead to complications such as scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience skeletal anomalies, including delayed closure of the soft spot on the head and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs ongoing monitoring for her heart condition and falls more often than her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may require periodic monitoring for their heart condition, and some may have tethered cord, which could lead to complications such as pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Additionally, palatal abnormalities and undescended testes should be kept under observation.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and speech delays, with some experiencing subtle palate problems and squint (astigmatism).

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away and turns the TV up really loud, indicating potential hearing or eye issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are weak and can decay easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not as good at sports as other kids, tripping and falling more often, suggesting potential educational challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have entered puberty within the typical age range, while others may need more support in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not as good at sports as other kids, tripping and falling more often, suggesting potential behavioral or developmental differences.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

a) Regular dental check-ups.

g) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
h) Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and behavioural therapy.

Parent: Lately, our child has complaned about tooth sensitivity when consuming cold foods or drinks. It seems to cause him significant discomfort and pain. We've taken him to see a dentist who suggested a few possible reasons and treatments to alleviate this symptom.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Unfortunately, during a routine check-up, a septal defect was discovered in his heart. The cardioligist explained it's a hole between the chambers of the heart that didn't close the way it should after birth. We're currently exploring options for corrective surgery and managing the situation closely with medication and lifestyle adjustments.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Observing our child's physical development and coordination skills, we've noticed he seems less coordinated when performing certain movements compared to peers of the same age. While it might not be a severe concern at this stage, we believe monitoring and possibly seeking occupational therapy could help improve these skills over time.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Interestingly, our child often shows a preference against eating specific types of food which sometimes leads to mealtime struggles. Despite offering a variet of healthy options, he tends to stick to a limited range of foods he finds acceptable. This can be challenging but we manage by ensuring nutritional balance through supplements when necessary.

Parent: One notable feature is that our child has shorter fingers than average which can affect dexterity and fine motor skills. # CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in his heart, which is a hole between the chambers of the heart that didn't close properly after birth. This requires close monitoring and potential surgical intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others can be managed with medication and lifestyle adjustments.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and has a limited range of acceptable foods, leading to mealtime struggles. Despite offering a varied diet, he prefers certain types of food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding. Lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting, and some may need longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has neurological development delays, including less coordinated movement compared to peers. Monitoring and potentially seeking occupational therapy could help improve his skills over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments. In a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Regular hearing reviews are recommended to ensure proper hearing development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had issues with fluid in the ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss. Regular monitoring and treatment of fluid buildup is important.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (cross-eyed), which can affect his ability to focus and coordinate his eyes. Regular eye checks are recommended to address these issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems like astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia). Regular eye examinations are crucial to detect and manage these conditions effectively.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods or drinks, indicating potential dental issues. Regular dental care is essential to prevent further complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can be a recurring issue for many individuals with KBG syndrome, affecting mealtime experiences and potentially impacting overall nutrition intake.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delay and behavioral differences, which may impact his academic performance and social interactions. However, with appropriate support and resources, he can make progress in mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome typically need additional support in school, including EHCP plans, and some may require specialized settings. However, many adults with the condition have gone on to lead fulfilling lives outside of education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delay and behavioral differences, including speech delay and difficulty making himself understood. Early intervention therapies such as physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy can provide benefits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often experience speech delay, and some may develop myopathy, a condition characterized by weak muscles and reduced muscle tone. Monitoring and supporting these aspects through a multidisciplinary approach can help mitigate some effects.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Regular monitoring and corrective measures under the guidance of a specialist can help manage this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait. Management strategies, including medication and physical therapy, may be beneficial.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, periodic eye checks, and consideration for cardiac, neurological, and orthopedic evaluations based on his specific needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may require ongoing monitoring for heart conditions, neurological conditions, palatal abnormalities, and other related issues. Regular assessments by specialists can help identify and address these conditions early, ensuring timely interventions to minimize morbidity and promote optimal health and development. # CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valvular abnormality in his heart, which is a significant concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often refuses to eat certain foods and becomes picky about what he eats, leading to feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with clarity when trying to talk, resulting in unclear sentences and difficulty understanding what he's trying to say.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have speech delay, and hearing loss and subtle palate problems can worsen speech delay.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of tooth sensitivity when consuming cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has complained about tooth sensitivity, especially with cold food and drink.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and struggles with clarity when trying to communicate, which impacts his ability to express himself effectively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though some go to a mainstream primary school, and some may require more support and some benefit from a specialist setting.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated when trying to communicate and struggles with clarity, which leads to difficulties in expressing himself and making himself understood.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Babies with KBG syndrome may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle), and some individuals with KBG syndrome have shorter fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups, and if anything is found, it does not need to be repeated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may require periodic monitoring for heart conditions, tethered cord, and palatal abnormalities, and regular dental care is essential.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Honestly, I'm overwhelmed with all the appointments and tests... but yes, his vision. He has myopia, and it's been a challenge getting him to wear his glasses consistently.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Oh gosh, sorry... yes, the hearing. He gets really frustrated in noisy environments, like malls or playgrounds. It's hard to calm him down when he's overstimulated.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Tooth sensitivity... yeah. He complains a lot when he eats cold foods, like ice cream or frozen yogurts. We try to avoid those things now.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The heart... right. He needs regular check-ups with the cardiologist because of some concerns they found. I'm not entirely sure what it all means, but we go to the appointments and follow their advice.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally... he's just taken a bit longer to hit some milestones, like walking or sitting. But he's getting therer slowly.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding was tough at first. He had trouble latching on and would spit up a lot. We worked with a specialist to get him eating properly, though.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: There's the thing with his fonanelle... it didn't close properly for a while, and we had to go back for more surgeries. That's been the worst part, really.
